surviving_claim: for the tested single-writer fixed-page primary, forced C->2C migration across C={32,2048,131072,4194304} preserved exact pre/post process-crash visibility while newly appended physical state remained operation-local rather than capacity-addressed. Recovery derived the committed frontier from two superblock reads and removed all uncommitted file-length residue without generation-page scan, mapping-node scan, or logical redo.
non_claims: the process-crash experiment is not a hardware power-loss, torn-sector, drive-cache, or filesystem-journal correctness proof
user-space pread/pwrite counts are not storage-device I/O bounds
the experiment is single-writer and does not establish arbitrary multi-writer, distributed, or replicated correctness
the fixed eight-level radix namespace is not mathematically unbounded
total mapping metadata is not constant with materialized segment count
ftruncate convergence is a file-length result, not a filesystem allocated-block reclamation guarantee
radix-node split or overflow behavior near the one-page JSON record limit is not tested in v0.30
